name: Underwater cable
summary: A cable section marked as laid under water, such as a river crossing, offshore export cable or lake crossing.
description: The underwater cable form identifies a section laid on or beneath a water bed. It appears on offshore wind export and array diagrams, island interconnectors and river crossings. The mark is a route indicator, so it sits on the cable line rather than replacing it.

Submarine cables usually have armour, longer lengths and different charging current from land cables, but the symbol carries none of that information. Transition joints at the landfall and the cable schedule supply those details. Where reactive compensation is fitted to a long submarine section, it appears as separate reactor symbols.
readingNotes: Locate the landfall transition joints at each end.
Check whether shunt compensation is shown for long sections.
distinction: An underwater cable is laid in or under water; an underground cable is buried on land.
